plan.title: Gender Improvement Comparison
plan.subtitle: Do girls and boys improve equally in physical fitness?

panels.title: Total baseline children
panels.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM baseline

panels.title: Total endline children
panels.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM endline

panels.title: Baseline shuttle run by gender
panels.sql: SELECT "Gender" AS gender, AVG("Shuttle run sec") AS avg_shuttle FROM baseline GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2

panels.title: Endline shuttle run by gender
panels.sql: SELECT "Gender" AS gender, AVG("Shuttle run sec") AS avg_shuttle FROM endline GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2

plan.narrative: The dashboard shows the total number of children at baseline ({{p1.n}}) and at endline ({{p2.n}}). The bar charts compare the average shuttle run time for girls and boys at each stage. A lower shuttle run time indicates better performance. By comparing the two bars for each gender, we can assess whether the improvement from baseline to endline is similar for girls and boys. If the reduction in shuttle run time is roughly the same for both genders, it suggests that they are improving equally. If one gender shows a larger improvement, that indicates a disparity in progress.
